title: Cognitive Reframing (Challenging Cognitive Distortions)
content:
Cognitive reframing guides you to examine automatic negative thoughts:
1. Identify the Automatic Thought: e.g., 'I will mess everything up and fail.'
2. Check the Evidence: What real facts support this? What facts contradict it?
3. Identify the Distortion: Is this catastrophizing, black-and-white thinking, or mind-reading?
4. Craft a Balanced Alternative: 'This is challenging, but I have navigated tough moments before, and doing my best is enough.'

title: The Worry Tree & Postponement Technique
content:
When caught in loops of 'what-if' thoughts:
1. Ask: 'Is this worry something I have direct control over right now?'
2. If YES: Identify one small, actionable step you can take today. Write it down, then gently shift focus to the next task.
3. If NO: Recognize that worrying does not change the outcome. Acknowledge the thought without judgment, imagine placing it in a jar to look at during a designated 10-minute 'worry time' later, and return to the present moment.

title: Mindful Self-Compassion Break (Dr. Kristin Neff)
content:
A 3-step self-compassion practice for moments of emotional distress:
1. Mindfulness: Place your hand on your heart or stomach and say: 'This is a moment of suffering / This hurts.'
2. Common Humanity: Remind yourself: 'Suffering and struggling are part of being human. I am not weird or alone in feeling this.'
3. Kindness: Say to yourself: 'May I be kind to myself in this moment. May I give myself the patience and grace I need.'
